lines.japanese: 「ところで、細川玉木先生の名誉挽回を賭けた三作目は、いつごろ出るんすかね」
lines.english: “By the way, when do you think Tamaki Hosokawa will get a third book—a chance to redeem herself?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ……少なくとも、うちからは出ないんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “Who knows... At the very least, I doubt we'll be publishing it.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そうなんすか？　じゃあ他社さんから？」
lines.english: “Really? Will another company publish it, then?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、ていうか……いちおう原稿は届いてるらしいんだけど、うちの担当者に」
lines.english: “Hmm. More to the point... Apparently her editor here does have a manuscript.”

lines.japanese: 「え、うそ、新作の？」
lines.english: “What? Seriously? A new book?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。届いたって言うか、持ち込まれたって言うのかな。発注してなかったのに、彼女の方から『どうでしょうこれ』みたいな感じで置いてったんだって」
lines.english: “Yes. Though rather than saying it arrived, perhaps I should say she brought it in. Nobody commissioned it. She simply came in, said something like, ‘What do you think of this?’ and left it with them.”

lines.japanese: 「持ち込み、ですか……」
lines.english: “She brought them an unsolicited manuscript...”

lines.japanese: ふうん。一度デビューしたひとでも、そういうのするんだ。
lines.english: Huh. So even someone who had already debuted still did that sort of thing.

lines.japanese: 「つい最近の話だよ。えっと……たしか田辺君が集稿で中村先生のとこ行ってる日だから……先週の土曜か」
lines.english: “It was quite recent. Let's see... It was the day Tanabe went to collect Nakamura's manuscript... Last Saturday, I think.”

lines.japanese: 先週の土曜……。
lines.english: Last Saturday...

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ちょうど俺が前回ここに来た日っすね」
lines.english: “Oh. That was the day I was here last.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ほんとだ。そういえばそうだね」
lines.english: “Oh, you're right. Come to think of it, it was.”

lines.japanese: ……ん？　ってことは？
lines.english: ...Hm? In that case...

lines.japanese: すなわち、俺が初めて日和子さんと会った日だ。
lines.english: That was the day I first met Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: そっか。あのとき彼女が一階のコーヒー屋さんにいたのは、担当さんに会う前か後だったんだな。
lines.english: I see. Then when I saw her at the coffee shop downstairs, she had either been about to meet her editor or had just finished doing so.

lines.japanese: ああ、だからあんなに……。
lines.english: Ah. That explained why she had been so...

lines.japanese: 「うーん、なるほど……ま、でも要するに、その持ちこまれた作品がイイカンジであれば、また出版されるってわけですよね」
lines.english: “Hmm, I see... Still, if the manuscript she brought in is good, they'll publish her again, right?”

lines.japanese: 「それはどうかなあ」
lines.english: “I wouldn't be so sure.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「編集者なんて大抵が暇な時間のない職業だし、いくつも抱えてる大事な仕事をほっぽってまで、必ず持ち込み原稿に目を通すとは限らないよ」
lines.english: “Editors are never short of work. They aren't guaranteed to set aside several important projects merely to read every unsolicited manuscript that lands on their desks.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ！　ちょ、そんな、いい加減な！」
lines.english: “What!? Wait, that's horribly irresponsible!”

lines.japanese: 「あのねえ、いい加減とかじゃなくて」
lines.english: “Listen. It isn't a matter of being irresponsible.”

lines.japanese: 「分かるよ、その、細川玉木ちゃんが必死なのは分かるけど、でも全国には同じように必死な子が、他にいくらだっているんだよ？」
lines.english: “I understand that Tamaki Hosokawa is desperate. I do. But countless other young writers across the country are every bit as desperate.”

lines.japanese: 「彼女は一度チャンスを潰しちゃったけど、まだその機会を一度だってもらってない子がいくらでもいるの。ね。細川タマちゃんを相手にするってことは、今度はその他の子たちをいい加減にするってことでしょ」
lines.english: “She got one chance and blew it. Plenty of others have never received even one. Giving Tamaki another shot means neglecting all those other writers instead, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「それは……そうなのかもしれないすけど……」
lines.english: “That... may be true, but...”

lines.japanese: 「あのね？　君にはまだ見えてないかもしれないけど、得てして世の中ってのはそういうものなの。ね。誰かが幸福になるってことは、誰かが不幸になるってことなの、分かる？」
lines.english: “Listen, all right? Perhaps you can't see it yet, but that is often how the world works. One person's happiness means another person's unhappiness. Do you understand?”

lines.japanese: 「わ、わか、分かる、っていうか、そんなの……」
lines.english: “I-I do. I mean, something like that...”

lines.japanese: 俺が反論を封じられて口ごもっていると、ふっと米田さんが肩を下ろしました。
lines.english: My objections silenced, I faltered. Yoneda suddenly let her shoulders fall.

lines.japanese: 「──だってさ」
lines.english: “—Or so they tell me.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「そーんな風に私、きのう沢井のヤロウに言われちまったい。ぶー」
lines.english: “That's exactly what that bastard Sawai said to me yesterday. Boo.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は拗ねた子供みたいに唇を突きだしました。
lines.english: She thrust out her lips like a sulking child.

lines.japanese: てことは、米田さんもいまの俺みたく、書籍部のどなたかに異を唱えてくれたってことです。
lines.english: Which meant Yoneda had objected on Hiyoko's behalf to someone in the book division, just as I had now.

lines.japanese: 「てゆか、細川タマちゃんも運が悪くてさ。彼女の担当がデビューから二人三脚で頑張ってきた編集者のままだったら、まだ情とか信頼があって優先されたのかもしれないけど、そのひと先月で寿退社しちゃっててー」
lines.english: “And Tamaki had rotten luck. If her editor were still the same person who'd worked beside her every step of the way since her debut, affection or trust might have earned her priority. But that editor left the company last month to get married.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、じゃあいまの編集さんは細川玉木になんも思い入れないひとなんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh. So her current editor doesn't feel anything in particular for Tamaki Hosokawa...”

lines.japanese: 「その言い方が適切かどうかは分かんないけど、他のゴマンといる新人に対してコレっちゅーアドバンテージはないのかもね。はー、厳しい世界」
lines.english: “I don't know if that's a fair way to put it, but she may have no particular advantage over the countless other newcomers out there. Whew. What a brutal world.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は机の縁に頬杖をついて、視線を床の下へ落としました。その先には、祥玄社文庫の編集部があるそうです。
lines.english: She propped her cheek in one hand at the edge of the desk and lowered her gaze through the floor. Shogensha's paperback editorial department was apparently directly beneath us.

lines.japanese: 俺も同じ方向を見つめて、しょんぼり「そうっすね」と呟きました。
lines.english: I stared in the same direction and murmured a dejected, ‘I suppose so.’

lines.japanese: きのう紀奈子さんが帰り際に「ひよちゃんも受かるといいね」なんて言ってたのは、きっとこのことだったのでしょう。なんとも浪人……訂正、受験生らしい表現です。
lines.english: When Kinako told Hiyoko yesterday that she hoped she would pass too, this must have been what she meant. What a thing for someone retaking her entrance exams—correction, taking them for the first time—to say.

lines.japanese: でも、いまの話を聞くかぎり結果はどうにも……はぁ。
lines.english: But from what I had just heard, the likely result seemed... hopeless. Sigh.

lines.japanese: ほんと、せつない話だなあ。
lines.english: It truly was a painful story.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そだ。それからさあ、話変わるけどー」
lines.english: “Oh, right. There was something else. Changing the subject...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんが椅子の上で足を組みながら言いました。話題転換のようですが、声のトーンはさらに低くなったような気がします。
lines.english: Yoneda crossed her legs in the chair as she spoke. It was a change of subject, but her voice seemed to sink lower still.

lines.japanese: 「この前、ここで千歳君に話したよねえ？　ネット中心に、カケルの悪い噂が広まってるって」
lines.english: “I told you about this here the other day, didn't I? The ugly rumors about Kakeru spreading online.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、あの子が、よくない連中と付きあってるとか」
lines.english: “You know. That he's been associating with some dangerous people.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、はいはい。そういえば、なんか変なカキコミいっぱい見せられましたね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Come to think of it, you showed me a heap of strange posts.”

lines.japanese: 「アレさー、最近とみに真実味を増してきてんだよねー」
lines.english: “Those rumors have been looking a great deal more credible lately.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。そうなんすか」
lines.english: “Really. Is that so?”

lines.japanese: 確認すると、米田さんはまぶたを伏せて頷きました。
lines.english: When I asked for confirmation, Yoneda lowered her eyelids and nodded.

lines.japanese: 「あのね、ちょっと前に、柳木原のガード下でチーマーみたいな集団同士のケンカがあったんだって」
lines.english: “Apparently two packs of old-school street punks got into a fight beneath the railway tracks in Yanagihara a little while ago.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そのチーマーっていう生き物、まだ日本に生息してたんですか」
lines.english: “Those creatures still exist in Japan?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃあ、だってほら。愚連隊、暴走族、ストリートギャング？　スタイルはその都度変わってっても、徒党を組みたがるやんちゃ坊主っていうのは、この先何百年経っても絶滅しないんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Of course. Street toughs, biker gangs, street gangs—the style keeps changing, but boys who want to form packs and run wild probably won't go extinct for another few hundred years.”

lines.japanese: 「歴史的にもさ、お侍の時代から傾奇者なんて不良小僧がいたわけでしょ。戦前戦後の学生運動だの政治運動だのも、実はノンポリのくせにとりあえずノリで暴れてたおにーちゃんとか、何気にいたと思うんだよねぇー」
lines.english: “Historically speaking, even the age of the samurai had flamboyant young toughs who dressed to shock. And among all those student and political movements before and after the war, I'm sure plenty of apolitical young men joined the violence simply because everyone else was doing it.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、ちょっと分かんないすけど……そんで？　その２１世紀の愚連隊がどーしたんすか？」
lines.english: “I'm not sure I follow... Anyway, what did this twenty-first-century street gang do?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、その中のひとりが──しかも中心人物っぽいのが、鳳凰寺カケルに似てたって報告いくつかあるんだよねぇ」
lines.english: “Several people have reported that one of them—and apparently the central figure—looked like Kakeru Hououji.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。でも、どうせまた、どっかのカケルくん嫌いな覆面さんのでっちあげなんじゃないすか？」
lines.english: “Huh. But isn't that probably another fabrication by some anonymous nobody who hates Kakeru?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん私も、最初はそう気楽に構えてたんだけど、実はその話が、上の耳にも入っちゃったみたいで」
lines.english: “That was how casually I took it at first. But apparently the story has reached the people upstairs.”

lines.japanese: 「上って、デスクさんとか編集長さんとかですか？」
lines.english: “Upstairs meaning the managing editor and editor in chief?”

lines.japanese: 「もっと上。祥玄社の役員の方々とか。わざわざダイレクトに通報しやがったやつがいんのよ」
lines.english: “Higher. Shogensha's executives. Some bastard went out of their way to report it directly to them.”

lines.japanese: うんざりした溜息を吐く米田さん。それからマウスを操作して、ディスプレイに見覚えのあるサイトを表示させました。
lines.english: Yoneda released a weary sigh. Then she worked the mouse and brought up a site I recognized on her monitor.

lines.japanese: 「あー、いたいた。たぶん犯人こいつ。ＨＮヨーゼフ」
lines.english: “Ah, there he is. This is probably our culprit. Username: Josef.”

lines.japanese: ゆっくりスクロールしてゆく掲示板に、俺は顔を近づけてみました。
lines.english: I leaned closer to the message board as she scrolled slowly down it.

lines.japanese: 米田さんの説明によると、ファッション誌のフレッシュな新人モデルについて語らうこの若い女の子向けのサイトに、きのう・おととい辺りから突如ヨーゼフなる場違いな人物が現れたと言います。
lines.english: According to Yoneda, the site was intended for young women to discuss fresh new models in fashion magazines. Then, sometime yesterday or the day before, a spectacularly out-of-place figure named Josef had suddenly appeared.

lines.japanese: その彼だか彼女だかは「愚かなる咎人を社会的に抹殺せよ」とか薄気味悪いことをのたまって、ひたすら鳳凰寺カケルの誹謗中傷を書きつらねたそうです。
lines.english: Whether man or woman, this person had proclaimed creepy things like ‘Erase the foolish transgressor from society,’ then poured out an endless stream of abuse against Kakeru Hououji.

lines.japanese: 「サイトの管理人が何度も何度も消してるみたいだけどね、削除されても規制されても懲りずに来るんだよ。ネットカフェとか渡りあるいてんのかな、すごい執念だよね」
lines.english: “The site administrator keeps deleting the posts, but it doesn't matter how often they're removed or blocked—Josef always comes back. Maybe they're moving from one internet café to another. You have to admire the obsession.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、なんかヴィジュアル系くさい言い回しで長々書いてありますけど……要するにどーゆーこと言ってんすかコレ」
lines.english: “Man, this goes on forever in the kind of overblown language you’d expect from a band in full stage makeup... What’s it actually saying?”

lines.japanese: 尋ねると、米田さんはその中の一文をニュース番組のアナウンサーみたいな口調で音読してくれました。
lines.english: When I asked, Yoneda read one passage aloud in the voice of a television news anchor.

lines.japanese: 「少年自警団を標榜し、区内の若者たちに暴力で威武を示す『柳木原フレイムバーズ』、通称ＹＦＢ。傘下組織８を含んだ総構成員数は三桁にものぼると思われる。その頂点に君臨するのが鳳凰寺カケル、こと鳳翔」
lines.english: “The Yanagihara Flame Birds, commonly known as the YFB, style themselves a youth vigilante corps and assert their power through violence against the young people of the district. Including eight subordinate organizations, their total membership is believed to reach three figures. At their summit reigns Kakeru Hououji—better known as Kakeru Otori.”

lines.japanese: 「カケルくんがあ？　まっさかあ！」
lines.english: “Kakeru? Nooo chance!”

lines.japanese: 「まさかだといいんだけどさあ」
lines.english: “I hope there's no chance.”

lines.japanese: 「で、こいつ、ご丁寧に参考サイトのリンクとかも貼ってくれちゃってさ。試しにいくつか回ってみたんだー。そしたら」
lines.english: “And this person was kind enough to include links to reference sites. I tried visiting a few of them, and...”

lines.japanese: カチカチッとニ回クリックして、俺に「見て」とアイコンタクト。
lines.english: Click, click. She pressed the mouse twice, then signaled with her eyes for me to look.

lines.japanese: 「少なくとも、その柳木原フレイムバーズっていう集団は実在するみたい」
lines.english: “At the very least, this organization called the Yanagihara Flame Birds appears to exist.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんが飛んだ先は、都会の暗部を照らしだすという趣旨で構成された、あるルポライターの私的なレポート記事でした。
lines.english: The page she opened was an independent report by a writer devoted to illuminating the city's underworld.

lines.japanese: まず目に付いたのが、一枚の不鮮明な画像。
lines.english: The first thing to catch my eye was a blurry photograph.

lines.japanese: 暗視カメラの緑がかった写真なので顔までは判別できないけれど、オーバーサイズのだぼついた服をまとったチェケラッチョな若者たちが、数人で固まって輪を作っていました。
lines.english: The greenish image came from a night-vision camera, so no faces could be distinguished. Several young men in oversized, baggy streetwear had gathered into a tight circle.

lines.japanese: 彼らが見下ろしているその輪の底は見えませんでしたが、敵対勢力の少年を取りかこんで私刑にかけている場面、のような説明文が添付されていました。
lines.english: I couldn't see what lay at the bottom of the circle they peered into. The caption, however, described the group as surrounding a boy from a rival faction and subjecting him to vigilante punishment.

lines.japanese: 「この子たち、自警団って名乗ってるでしょ。なんでかっていうと、柳木原の悪ガキ共を懲らしめるって大儀を掲げてんだって。でも結局、やってることは──」
lines.english: “They call themselves a vigilante corps, right? Apparently that's because they claim to punish the young delinquents of Yanagihara. But in the end, what they're doing is—”

lines.japanese: ぐるぐるぐる。米田さんはマウスで円を描いて「同じ穴のムジナ」というキャプションを強調しました。
lines.english: Round and round. Yoneda circled the mouse pointer to emphasize the caption: ‘Cut from the same cloth.’

lines.japanese: 「ふうん……なんてーか、遠い世界の話で、いまいちピンと来ないっすねえ」
lines.english: “Hmm... It all belongs to such a distant world that I can't quite make it feel real.”

lines.japanese: 「ね、それよりこれ。この背の高い子──これ千歳君、どう思う？」
lines.english: “Never mind that. Look here. This tall boy—what do you think, Chitose?”

lines.japanese: そして今度はカーソルではなく、人差し指で直に画面の中のひとりを叩きました。
lines.english: This time she used her index finger rather than the cursor, tapping one figure directly on the screen.

lines.japanese: 「こ、これは……」
lines.english: “This is...”

lines.japanese: 不鮮明な画像。なかば俯いた表情。いつものユルカジ・スタイルな彼とは完全に正反対の、派手かつ華美なお兄系ファッション。
lines.english: The image was blurred, his face half lowered. Instead of his usual loose, casual clothes, he wore a flashy, heavily accessorized rock-star look—the complete opposite of his normal style.

lines.japanese: と、分かりづらくさせる条件が重なっているので、確実なことは言えないけれど──
lines.english: With so many things making identification difficult, I could say nothing for certain. And yet—

lines.japanese: 「似て……ますねえ」
lines.english: “He does... look similar.”

lines.japanese: あえて「誰に」かは省きました。
lines.english: I deliberately omitted whom he resembled.

lines.japanese: 「だよねえ」
lines.english: “He does, doesn't he?”

lines.japanese: 米田さんも認めたくなさそうに頷きました。
lines.english: Yoneda nodded with equal reluctance.

lines.japanese: 「……ねえ。千歳君、友達でしょ。ちょっと聞いてみてよ」
lines.english: “Listen. You're his friend, aren't you? Ask him about it.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、俺っすか！」
lines.english: “What? Me!?”

lines.japanese: 頼むよう、と両手を合わせる米田さん。
lines.english: Please, she mouthed, pressing both hands together.

lines.japanese: 「んー、まあ、聞くだけならべつに……いいですけど……」
lines.english: “Hmm. Well, if all you want me to do is ask... I suppose I can...”

lines.japanese: 「あー、でもさー……いや、もしだよ、仮にだよ、仮にそうだとしたら。彼、なんて答えると思う？」
lines.english: “Oh, but... No, this is hypothetical. Purely hypothetical. Suppose it is him. What do you think he'll say?”

lines.japanese: 「『え、知らなかったの？』」
lines.english: “‘What? You didn't know?’”

lines.japanese: 「言う！　やつはそう言う！」
lines.english: “He will! That is exactly what he'll say!”

lines.japanese: 「『聞いてくれれば教えたのに』」
lines.english: “‘I would've told you if you'd asked.’”

lines.japanese: 「言う！　やつはそういう男だ！」
lines.english: “He will! That is exactly the kind of man he is!”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは両手で頭を掴み、あああとお嘆きになりました。
lines.english: Yoneda clutched her head in both hands and wailed.

lines.japanese: 「ちっくしょー、あのガキ、なんか隠してると思ったらこういうことだよもう！　だからいつも、こっちの仕事テキトーだったんだよ。いずれ発覚するって、長くは続けられないって、自分で分かってたんだ……」
lines.english: “Goddamn it! I knew that brat was hiding something, and this is what it was! That's why he never took our work seriously. He knew it would come out eventually—knew he couldn't keep modeling for long...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、やっぱりそーゆーのって、バレたらクビっすか」
lines.english: “So if it comes out, he really will be fired?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……あの子フリーだから、クビとは違うけど……まあ、うちとしては全面的に契約破棄しなきゃだよね。そのとき私の処遇は……あああ、謹慎三日ぐらいで済むといいなあ」
lines.english: “Yes... He's freelance, so ‘fired’ isn't quite the word... But our company would have to terminate every contract with him. And then what happens to me...? Ohhh, I hope I get away with three days' suspension.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに、もし彼が非行……非行？　ていうの？　の事実を認めなかったらどうなるんすかね」
lines.english: “Incidentally, what happens if he denies committing any acts of delinquency... delinquency? Is that what we call this?”

lines.japanese: 「まー認めなくても、このままじゃいつかは動かぬ証拠が出そうだから……そしたらやっぱ同じことかなあ」
lines.english: “Even if he denies it, at this rate hard proof will surface eventually... and then I suppose the outcome is the same.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、それでは、我々の取りうる最良の手は？」
lines.english: “Th-then what is the best course available to us?”

lines.japanese: 「可及的すみやかに足を洗わせ、将来事実が発覚した際はすべて『若気のいたり』で片付ける」
lines.english: “Make him leave the gang as quickly as possible, and if the truth ever emerges, dismiss the whole thing as youthful indiscretion.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、それだ……」
lines.english: “Th-that's it...”

lines.japanese: 俺は自信なさげに賛同しました。米田さんも俺以上に力を落とし、がっくりうなだれてしまいました。
lines.english: My agreement lacked conviction. Yoneda had lost even more strength than I had and now hung her head in despair.

lines.japanese: 「参ったなあ……作品性とか本人の性格から、なーんか問題ある子だとは思ってたけど……ああ、まさかこんな爆弾抱えてたとはなあ……」
lines.english: “What a mess... His work and his personality always made me think he was trouble somehow... But I never imagined he was carrying a bomb like this...”

lines.japanese: 「実はね、初めて軽部先輩に紹介されたときから、すでにほのかな予感はあったんだ……でもそれ以上になんか素質みたいの感じちゃったからさ、自分の中でうやむやにしちゃったんだよね」
lines.english: “The truth is, I had a faint premonition from the moment Karube first introduced us. But I sensed even more potential in him, so I blurred the concern inside my own head and let it go.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、まあ、警察のご厄介になって発覚とかじゃないですから。こんなん、言っちゃえばニュースじゃなくて、ただのスキャンダルですから」
lines.english: “W-well, it didn't come out because the police arrested him. Put that way, this isn't news. It's only a scandal.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうだよねえ？　ただ電脳世界の隅っこで小虫が騒いでるだけだよねえ？」
lines.english: “R-right? It's only a tiny insect making noise in one forgotten corner of cyberspace, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「そうっすよ！　ぜんぜん気にすることないっすよ！　いまんとこ」
lines.english: “Exactly! There's absolutely nothing to worry about! For now.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよね！　ぜんぜん気にすることないよねえ！　いまんとこ」
lines.english: “Exactly! Absolutely nothing to worry about! For now.”

lines.japanese: いまんとこ。
lines.english: For now.

lines.japanese: はぁぁ……不吉な言葉です……。
lines.english: Siiiigh... What ominous words...

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そういうわけだから千歳君」
lines.english: “So that's the situation, Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい？」
lines.english: “Y-yes?”

lines.japanese: 「カケルのこと、頼んだね。どこに出しても恥ずかしくない、清廉潔白な体にしてあげて」
lines.english: “I'm entrusting Kakeru to you. Clean him up until he's a spotless young man we can present anywhere without shame.”

lines.japanese: 「えええっ！　む、無理ですよそんな！　あの彼が、他人の言うことなんか聞くわけないじゃないですか！　しかもこんな……や、やなぎはら、ふれいむ、ばーず？」
lines.english: “What!? Th-that's impossible! Kakeru would never listen to another human being! And this... Y-Yanagihara Flame Birds?”

lines.japanese: 「ムリムリ！　ぜったいムリ！　こんなゴツくてハゲててガラの悪いひとたち、俺の手に負えないっすよ！　だって、なにこの目、喉アメ感覚で日常的にクスリとかキメてそうじゃないですか！」
lines.english: “No, no, impossible! Absolutely impossible! These men are built like tanks, bald, and terrifying! I can't handle them! Look at those eyes—they look like they pop drugs every day as casually as throat lozenges!”

lines.japanese: 「鷲介、行動する前から諦めちゃダメ！　この問題には私の減給、ヘタしたら首がかかってるんだからね！　あと一応カケルの将来とか」
lines.english: “Shusuke, you can't give up before you've even tried! My salary is riding on this, and possibly my job! Also Kakeru's future, technically.”

lines.japanese: 「優先順位がエゴ丸出し！」
lines.english: “Your priorities are naked self-interest!”

lines.japanese: 「てか米田さんこそ。ねえ？　ご自身の人生かかってんだったら、それこそ自分で行動する前から諦めちゃダメ！　じゃないですか」
lines.english: “More to the point, what about you, Yoneda? If your whole life depends on this, surely you're the one who can't give up before taking action!”

lines.japanese: 「ふん、いいよ、分かったよ。どうせね。二年前の私がここの内定取るのに、どれだけ汗と涙と男の誘いを流したか、アルバイト大好き千歳君には理解できないもんね」
lines.english: “Hmph. Fine. A part-time-work enthusiast like you could never understand how much sweat and how many tears I shed—and how many men I turned down—to win an offer from this company two years ago.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ来たっ！　来たよコレ！　モラトリアム人間の劣等感を苛む、四大卒のマインドアタック！」
lines.english: “There it is! The college graduate's psychic assault, striking at the inferiority complex of an overgrown adolescent!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、千歳君とも短い縁だったな、新しいライター探さなきゃ」
lines.english: “Sigh. Our acquaintance was brief, Chitose. I suppose I'd better find a new writer.”

lines.japanese: 「そして露骨な脅迫でたーっ！」
lines.english: “And now the naked threat!”
